dimensions.name: syntactic_validity
dimensions.notes: Valid PHP throughout. Correct TestCase extension, Guzzle Client usage, and PHPUnit assertion calls. No syntax issues.

dimensions.name: behavior_fidelity
dimensions.notes: testCannotDeletePaymentMethodWithCompletedOrder correctly targets the new 'complete' status boundary. testTokenWithSurroundingWhitespaceIsNormalised correctly exercises the new trim($token) path. Minor gap: does not assert the specific error message text returned on the completed-order block.

dimensions.name: coverage_delta
dimensions.notes: Two new test methods cover the two new code paths introduced by the diff. No previously-covered paths were regressed.

dimensions.name: assertion_quality
dimensions.notes: assertNotContains for 404/422 in the whitespace test is correct. The completed-order test's conditional body check on $body['error'] is good defensive practice. Weakness: testCannotDeletePaymentMethodWithCompletedOrder does not assert the response body message string directly.

dimensions.name: determinism
dimensions.notes: Tests depend on fixture tokens from $_ENV, which is correct practice. The 'completed order' fixture token is an assumption — if the test environment does not have a seeded completed order for this token, the test will trivially pass without exercising the block.

dimensions.name: syntactic_validity
dimensions.notes: Valid PHP. Correct namespace, TestCase extension, and Guzzle usage. All assertions use correct PHPUnit API.

dimensions.name: behavior_fidelity
dimensions.notes: testInvalidFormKeyReturnsJsonErrorWithoutException correctly targets the new logger.warning path and asserts both the HTTP status and the response shape. Does not (and cannot easily) assert the log entry itself — acceptable for an API-level test.

dimensions.name: coverage_delta
dimensions.notes: Adds one new test method covering the invalid-form-key path with the new logging block. Existing tests remain valid against the updated source.

dimensions.name: assertion_quality
dimensions.notes: assertFalse($body['success']) is precise. assertIsArray for JSON body is correct. The comment explaining why the 500-guard assertion matters (logger misconfiguration) is appropriately documented.

dimensions.name: determinism
dimensions.notes: Intentionally omitting form_key to trigger the path is a reliable approach. Minor concern: some Magento configurations auto-generate form keys, which could cause the test to exercise the success path instead — consider adding an explicit invalid form_key value.
